title: /doctor cleanup briefly emptied ~/.claude/settings.json via misplaced jq --args
details:
- **What happened:** While applying the approved /doctor cleanup, the model ran `jq --arg … --args '<filter>' "$S" <names…> > "$T"`; with `--args` placed before the filter, jq consumed the settings path as a positional string and read stdin (empty), producing an empty temp file. The guard `jq empty "$T"` accepts empty input, so `cp "$T" "$S"` overwrote `~/.claude/settings.json` with 0 bytes. Detected on the next verification read; restored from the mktemp backup made in the same command and reapplied correctly (`file --args names`) with an `-s`/`-e` non-empty check. Expected: the write guard should have rejected empty output.
- **What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model.
- **Repro:** `jq --args 'filter' file a b > out; jq empty out && cp out file` — `jq empty` on empty input exits 0.
- **Evidence:** session 2026-10-13, /doctor run in ~/projects/ru-stl; backup path printed as `claude-settings-backup.XXXXXX.XlYldQ97r5` in the mktemp dir.
- **Cause:** jq `--args` must follow the input file; verified in-session by the corrected command producing the expected 7,641-byte file.
